Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ConnectSphere Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Chen, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ConnectSphere's Q3 earnings call. Joining me today are David Miller, CEO; Emily Carter, CFO; Michael Lee, CTO; Robert Jones, Chief Revenue Officer; Jessica Davis, Chief Product Officer; and Laura Garcia, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to David Miller.

David Miller:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on ConnectSphere's performance for Q3. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our SynergyCloud and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on seven key areas: Operating Margin, Capital Allocation, Rule of 40, Average Contract Value, Operating Expense Breakdown, Churn Analysis, and Sales Efficiency.

Okay, good morning everyone, and thank you for joining us for our Q3 2024 earnings call. As always, I'm joined by Emily Carter, our CFO. I'll be focusing on our operating margin performance today. In Q3 2024, we achieved an operating margin of 18.5%, a significant improvement compared to the 15.2% we reported in Q3 2023 and slightly above the 18% we projected in our guidance last quarter. This represents consecutive quarters of operating margin expansion and demonstrates the effectiveness of our operational efficiency initiatives. Our primary driver continues to be the robust growth in our subscription revenue, which increased by 28% year-over-year. This growth is fueled by strong adoption of our flagship product, "SynergyCloud," our integrated CRM, marketing automation, and sales enablement platform, particularly within the mid-market segment, where we are seeing significant displacements of legacy systems like Salesforce and HubSpot amongst companies looking for more integrated cost-effective solutions. The growth engine is further enhanced by our expansion into the EMEA region. Our net revenue retention rate remained healthy at 118%, indicating successful upselling and cross-selling of additional modules within our existing customer base. The new "SynergyAI" add-on, which leverages generative AI for automated content creation and personalized customer engagement, is proving to be a key driver for upsell. We've seen 35% of our existing SynergyCloud customers adopt SynergyAI this quarter. As revenue scales, we are realizing economies of scale across several key areas. Specifically in our cloud infrastructure costs, we've negotiated more favorable pricing with AWS and Azure leveraging our increased commitment and volume. While we continue to invest heavily in R&D to maintain our competitive edge and innovate, we have implemented several initiatives to improve R&D efficiency, including shifting to a more agile development methodology, resulting in faster iteration cycles and reduced development time for new features. Our engineering teams are now using tools like Jira and Confluence more effectively to streamline collaboration and track progress, resulting in a 15% increase in code deployment velocity. We're also piloting AI-powered code analysis tools to identify and eliminate inefficiencies in our codebase, leading to reduced compute costs and improved application performance. We expect to see the full impact of this initiative in the coming quarters. We've strategically outsourced certain non-core development tasks, such as front-end development and testing, to specialized vendors, allowing our internal teams to focus on strategic initiatives. We've also invested in sales enablement tools and training programs to improve sales productivity. Our sales reps are now leveraging data-driven insights to identify and target high-potential leads, resulting in higher conversion rates. We've also seen an increase in average deal size as our sales team becomes more adept at selling the value of our integrated platform. We're continuously optimizing our marketing spend by focusing on channels with the highest ROI. For example, we've shifted more of our budget towards targeted digital marketing campaigns and away from less effective traditional channels. We're also leveraging marketing automation tools to nurture leads and personalize customer engagement. While the EMEA region is experiencing strong revenue growth, we are carefully managing sales and marketing costs in this region, adopting a partner-led sales model in certain countries and focusing on localized marketing campaigns to ensure cost-effectiveness. We are focused on streamlining our G&A functions and leveraging technology to automate manual processes. This includes implementing a cloud-based finance and accounting system, which has automated many manual tasks and improved the accuracy of our financial reporting, and piloting an AI-powered accounts payable automation solution, which is expected to reduce processing costs and improve efficiency. As I mentioned earlier, SynergyCloud is proving to be a compelling alternative to fragmented solutions from vendors like Salesforce and HubSpot. Our integrated platform allows customers to consolidate their CRM, marketing automation, and sales enablement tools into a single, unified system, reducing costs and improving efficiency. This platform consolidation trend is driving strong demand for SynergyCloud. We are strategically focused on the mid-market segment, where we believe we have a significant competitive advantage. Our platform is specifically designed to meet the needs of mid-sized businesses, and our pricing is more competitive than that of larger vendors. We are exploring opportunities to expand into specific vertical markets, such as healthcare and financial services. By tailoring our platform to the specific needs of these industries, we can increase our market share and drive revenue growth.

Okay, let's dive into our capital allocation strategy. As you know, disciplined capital allocation is paramount to driving sustainable, long-term shareholder value in the dynamic SaaS landscape. Today, I'll outline our approach, focusing on investments, acquisitions, and returns to shareholders, all within the context of our current growth trajectory and market opportunities. Our capital allocation framework prioritizes a balanced approach. We aim to reinvest in organic growth, as this is our primary focus. We believe the most efficient way to generate returns is through internal innovation and expansion of our existing products and services. We also seek strategically aligned acquisitions that accelerate our market position, add complementary technologies, or expand our geographic reach. We are disciplined in our valuation approach, prioritizing targets that offer compelling synergies and clear paths to integration. While growth investments remain our priority, we acknowledge the importance of returning capital to shareholders when appropriate, primarily through share repurchases. We are significantly increasing our R&D investment, projecting a 28% increase year-over-year, reaching $220 million for the upcoming fiscal year. $75 million is earmarked for integrating advanced AI and machine learning capabilities across our core product suite, "SynergySuite," specifically focusing on predictive analytics for customer churn, personalized user experiences, and automated workflow optimization. This is crucial to compete with emerging players like DataRobot and C3.ai who are rapidly embedding AI into their platforms. We are seeing a 15% higher ACV and a 20% reduction in churn for customers who have adopted our initial AI-powered features released in Q4. $50 million is dedicated to accelerating the migration of our legacy modules to a fully cloud-native architecture leveraging Kubernetes and serverless technologies on AWS and Azure. This improves scalability, resilience, and reduces infrastructure costs by an estimated 18% over the next three years. We believe this is critical to remain competitive with cloud-native SaaS solutions from companies like Snowflake or Datadog. $35 million is allocated to bolster our security infrastructure and data privacy compliance, including investments in threat detection, incident response, and adherence to GDPR, CCPA, and emerging data privacy regulations. This is a non-negotiable priority given the increasing threat landscape and our commitment to data security. We also plan to implement a zero-trust security model across our organization. $20 million is allocated to optimize our platform for mobile devices, recognizing the growing trend of remote work and distributed teams. We are focusing on building native iOS and Android apps with enhanced offline capabilities and seamless integration with our desktop platform. $40 million is being allocated to push compute power closer to the edge, allowing our software to perform real-time analysis of data generated by IoT devices and other edge sources. This is especially useful for our manufacturing and logistics clients. We are increasing our Sales & Marketing spend by 22% to $315 million. We are investing heavily in expanding our sales and marketing presence in the EMEA region, specifically targeting Germany and France. We are opening new offices in Berlin and Paris, hiring local sales teams, and tailoring our marketing campaigns to local market needs. We see significant untapped potential in this region, but recognize the need for a localized approach. We are allocating $70 million specifically for this EMEA expansion, including hiring country managers and building a strong partner ecosystem. We are investing $30 million to develop strategic partnerships with leading system integrators like Accenture and Deloitte, as well as cloud platform providers like AWS and Azure. These partnerships will help us expand our reach, accelerate adoption of our platform, and provide value-added services to our customers. We are seeing a 30% increase in deal size and a 25% faster sales cycle when working with our strategic partners. The remaining budget is allocated to enhancing our content marketing efforts, optimizing our website for lead generation, and investing in digital advertising campaigns to reach a wider audience. We are focusing on creating high-quality content that educates and engages our target audience, and using data analytics to optimize our marketing campaigns for maximum ROI. We are investing heavily in ABM, focusing on targeting high-value enterprise accounts with personalized marketing messages and sales outreach. This is showing early signs of success, with a 40% increase in pipeline for targeted ABM accounts. We maintain a disciplined approach to M&A, focusing on acquisitions that are strategically aligned with our long-term goals. The target company must complement our existing product portfolio, expand our market reach, or add valuable new technologies, have a strong financial track record, with a history of revenue growth, profitability, and positive cash flow, and have a culture that is compatible with our own, with a focus on innovation, customer satisfaction, and employee engagement. We acquired DataLeap, a small but innovative company specializing in data visualization and analytics, for $80 million in cash and stock. DataLeap's technology has been successfully integrated into SynergySuite, enhancing our platform's reporting and analytics capabilities and providing our customers with deeper insights into their data. We anticipate DataLeap adding approximately $15 million in ARR in the next fiscal year and contributing to a 5% increase in our overall customer retention rate. We are currently evaluating several potential acquisition targets in the areas of low-code/no-code development, cybersecurity solutions, and AI-Powered Automation. While we prioritize organic growth and strategic M&A, we also recognize the importance of returning capital to shareholders when appropriate. Given our strong cash flow generation, we are announcing a $50 million share repurchase program authorized by the Board. This program will be executed opportunistically, taking into account market conditions and our overall capital allocation priorities. We believe this program demonstrates our confidence in the long-term prospects of the company and our commitment to creating value for our shareholders. We will continually evaluate the appropriateness of future share repurchase programs based on our financial performance and market conditions. We are targeting a revenue growth rate of 25-30% for the upcoming fiscal year. We expect our gross margin to remain stable at around 75-78%. We are targeting an operating margin of 15-18%, reflecting our continued investments in growth. We expect to generate strong free cash flow, which will provide us with the flexibility to continue investing in our business and returning capital to shareholders.

Okay, everyone, let's turn to a key performance indicator that many of you have been closely monitoring: the Rule of 40. As you know, this metric provides a quick and valuable snapshot of our company's balanced growth and profitability. It's calculated by simply adding our revenue growth rate to our profit margin. For Q3 2024, our Rule of 40 score is 43%. This represents a strong performance and demonstrates a healthy balance between expansion and financial discipline. We achieved a year-over-year revenue growth rate of 31%. This growth is primarily driven by continued adoption of our flagship product, "Synergy Suite", our AI-powered, cloud-based project management and collaboration platform, continues to be a major driver. We're seeing strong uptake, particularly among mid-sized enterprises (500-2000 employees) looking for scalable and integrated solutions to replace legacy systems like Jira and disparate spreadsheets. We've observed a 15% increase in the average contract value (ACV) for Synergy Suite compared to Q3 2023, indicating that customers are recognizing and willing to pay for the enhanced value proposition. Our investments in localized sales and support infrastructure in the Asia-Pacific region are yielding positive results. Revenue from APAC grew by 45% year-over-year. We're seeing particularly strong demand in Australia and Singapore, where businesses are rapidly adopting cloud-based solutions. We are also starting to see traction in the Japanese market, although the sales cycles are longer than in other regions. Our integration partnerships with leading CRM providers like Salesforce and HubSpot are also contributing to growth. We're seeing customers bundle Synergy Suite with their existing CRM investments, creating a more seamless workflow and driving higher customer lifetime value (CLTV). We will be anouncing a new partnership with a major PaaS provider like AWS or Azure next quarter. Our non-GAAP operating profit margin for Q3 is 12%. This reflects our commitment to operational efficiency and sustainable profitability despite the growth investments outlined above. Our gross margin remains healthy at 75%. This is attributable to the scalability of our SaaS model and our ongoing efforts to optimize our infrastructure costs. We are currently in the process of migrating our core infrastructure to more cost-effective AWS Graviton instances. While we continue to invest in sales and marketing to drive growth, we're laser-focused on improving efficiency. We are leveraging data analytics to identify and target high-potential leads, optimize our marketing campaigns, and improve our sales conversion rates. Our customer acquisition cost (CAC) payback period is currently at 14 months, which is healthy for our industry. We continue to invest heavily in research and development to maintain our competitive edge and drive future growth. Our R&D spending as a percentage of revenue is approximately 20%. This investment is focused on enhancing the capabilities of Synergy Suite, particularly in areas like AI-powered automation, predictive analytics, and integration with emerging technologies. This includes the development of a new low-code/no-code workflow automation engine, internally codenamed "Project Nightingale," which is slated for beta release in Q1 2025. While we are pleased with our Q3 performance, we are also mindful of the evolving macroeconomic environment. We are seeing increased scrutiny of software spending among some of our larger enterprise clients, particularly in the financial services sector. To mitigate this, we are focusing on demonstrating the clear ROI of our solutions and providing flexible pricing options. Looking ahead, we remain committed to achieving a Rule of 40 score of 40% or higher on a consistent basis. Our strategic priorities include accelerating growth in key markets, enhancing product innovation, driving operational efficiency, and considering strategic opportunities.

Okay, let's dive into the Average Contract Value (ACV) performance for this quarter and the trends we're observing. As we move into the discussion of key performance indicators, let's focus on Average Contract Value, or ACV. As you know, ACV is a crucial metric for us, representing the average revenue recognized from a single customer contract over a 12-month period. Understanding its trends is paramount to gauging the health and strategic direction of our business. For Q3 2024, our overall ACV stood at $48,500, representing a 12% increase year-over-year compared to Q3 2023's $43,300. This growth is a positive indicator of our ability to land larger deals and up-sell existing customers. The ACV for new customer contracts reached $35,000, a 7% increase from the $32,700 reported in Q3 2023. This growth in new customer ACV suggests that our product is resonating with larger organizations from the outset and that our initial penetration strategy is working. Expansion ACV, representing the increased value of contracts from existing customers through upselling and cross-selling, reached $62,000, marking a 15% increase compared to the $54,000 in Q3 2023. This is a significant achievement and underscores the success of our customer success initiatives and the value customers are realizing from expanded product adoption. We have strategically shifted our focus towards larger enterprise clients, particularly in the financial services and healthcare sectors. These organizations typically require more comprehensive solutions and have larger budgets. Our recent acquisition of "DataStream Analytics," a real-time data processing platform, has allowed us to offer a more robust and integrated solution, leading to higher ACVs in these segments. The introduction of our "Premium" and "Enterprise" tiers, offering advanced features like AI-powered predictive analytics and enhanced security protocols, has significantly boosted ACV. Approximately 35% of new customers are now opting for these higher-tier offerings, compared to 25% in Q2. We are seeing a strong correlation between premium tier adoption and customer satisfaction, as these features directly address critical business challenges. Our platform strategy, aimed at providing a unified suite of tools for operations (e.g., marketing automation, sales enablement, customer service), is driving significant value. Customers who adopt multiple modules within our platform have a significantly higher ACV (approximately 60% higher) compared to those using a single product. This highlights the importance of our integrated approach and the stickiness of our platform. We've implemented a value-based pricing model that aligns our pricing with the tangible business outcomes our customers achieve. This allows us to capture a greater share of the value we deliver and justify higher ACVs, particularly for customers in industries like e-commerce, where our solutions directly impact revenue generation. Our channel partner program, particularly with system integrators like Accenture and Deloitte, has been instrumental in landing larger, more complex deals. These partners have the expertise to implement and integrate our solutions into complex enterprise environments, driving higher ACV and broader adoption. North America remains our largest market and continues to show healthy ACV growth, driven by strong demand from the financial services and healthcare sectors. We are seeing particularly strong ACV growth in the DACH region (Germany, Austria, Switzerland), driven by the adoption of our enterprise-grade security features. However, the macroeconomic climate in the UK has led to more cautious spending and slightly lower ACV growth compared to other regions. While ACV growth in APAC is strong, particularly in Australia and Singapore, the average ACV is still lower compared to North America and EMEA. This is due to a different mix of customers and a higher proportion of smaller businesses in the region. We are investing in localized marketing and sales efforts to target larger enterprises in APAC and increase ACV in the long term. We are continuously investing in our product to enhance its value and drive further ACV growth. Key initiatives include integrating AI and machine learning across our platform to automate tasks, improve decision-making, and personalize customer experiences, expanding our integration ecosystem to seamlessly connect with other popular business applications, such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, Workday, and ServiceNow, and prioritizing mobile accessibility and functionality to cater to the growing demand for on-the-go access to our solutions.

Okay, let's dive into the operating expense breakdown. As always, all figures are presented in USD millions unless otherwise stated. Let's turn our attention to our operating expense breakdown for Q2 2024. I'll be discussing trends in Research & Development (R&D), Sales & Marketing (S&M), and General & Administrative (G&A) expenses, and providing some context around these figures. We're operating in a SaaS market that's showing signs of both continued growth and increased scrutiny. While demand for cloud-based solutions remains strong, particularly in areas like AI-powered automation, cybersecurity, and platform engineering, customers are increasingly focused on demonstrating ROI and optimizing their existing SaaS investments. This necessitates a more targeted and efficient approach to our operating expenses. R&D expense for Q2 2024 was $75 million, representing 22% of revenue, compared to $60 million in Q2 2023, representing 20% of revenue, a year-over-year growth of 25%. The primary driver for the increased R&D spend is our accelerated investment in AI and machine learning capabilities across our product suite. Specifically, we're heavily involved in integrating generative AI features across our core platform, which is directly impacting development costs. This includes "Project Athena", which focuses on embedding AI-powered predictive analytics into our core platform, enabling customers to proactively identify potential issues and optimize performance. We've seen promising results in the beta program, with users reporting a 15-20% reduction in downtime. We're also exploring AI-assisted code generation to accelerate the development of new features and improve developer productivity. A significant portion of our R&D budget is dedicated to bolstering our cybersecurity infrastructure, particularly in light of recent high-profile attacks targeting SaaS providers. This includes investing in advanced threat detection and prevention systems, as well as ongoing security audits and penetration testing. We are also seeing an increase in investment to support our containerization and microservices architecture to improve scalability and resilience. We're expanding our R&D presence in Eastern Europe to tap into a strong talent pool and reduce overall labor costs. This expansion will contribute to increased R&D expenses in the short term but will provide cost advantages in the long run. S&M expense for Q2 2024 was $110 million, representing 32% of revenue, compared to $90 million in Q2 2023, representing 30% of revenue, a year-over-year growth of 22%. We are shifting our sales and marketing strategy towards a more focused ABM approach, targeting high-value enterprise accounts. This requires a more personalized and data-driven approach to marketing, which is driving up our marketing expenses. We are actively expanding into new verticals, such as the healthcare and financial services industries. This requires investment in specialized sales teams, marketing campaigns tailored to these industries, and compliance certifications. While we're still investing in digital marketing, we're focusing on optimizing our campaigns to improve conversion rates and reduce customer acquisition costs (CAC). We are leveraging data analytics to identify the most effective channels and messaging. Investing in sales enablement tools and training to equip our sales team with the necessary resources and knowledge to effectively sell our solutions, including platforms like SalesLoft and Gong.io to standardize and optimize sales processes. We see strong growth opportunities in the APAC region, particularly in countries like India and Australia. However, the cost of customer acquisition in these markets is relatively high due to the need for localized marketing campaigns and sales teams. G&A expense for Q2 2024 was $35 million, representing 10% of revenue, compared to $30 million in Q2 2023, representing 10% of revenue, a year-over-year growth of 16.7%. We are facing increased compliance costs due to evolving regulations, particularly around data privacy and cybersecurity. As our company grows, we need to invest in scaling our infrastructure, including IT systems, HR processes, and financial reporting. As a publicly traded company, we incur higher costs related to investor relations, board fees, and Sarbanes-Oxley compliance. We continue to invest in automation of back-office functions such as accounts payable and contract management to improve efficiency and reduce headcount related expenses.

Okay, let's dive into churn analysis. As we all know, in the SaaS world, retaining customers is just as, if not more, crucial than acquiring new ones. Today, I'll be providing an in-depth look at our churn performance, the drivers behind it, and the strategies we're implementing to improve retention. Our overall Gross Dollar Retention (GDR) sits at 92%, which, while respectable, is slightly below our target of 94% and lags behind leading SaaS players like Atlassian, which regularly clocks in at 95%+ for their core products like Jira. Churn increased slightly this quarter, primarily attributed to macroeconomic headwinds impacting SMB clients and feature gaps in our enterprise-level platform. We are actively addressing these challenges through targeted product development, enhanced customer success initiatives, and adjusted pricing strategies. Our Logo Churn Rate is 7.8% with a Net Dollar Retention (NDR) of 115%. While our NDR remains healthy, masking some of the churn issues, we need to address the underlying problems to ensure long-term, sustainable growth. We've identified several key reasons for customer churn, segmented by customer size and region. This segment is highly sensitive to economic fluctuations. With rising inflation and potential recessionary pressures, many SMBs are cutting costs, and unfortunately, SaaS tools are sometimes seen as discretionary expenses. We saw a spike in churn within the SMB segment in Q2, particularly in the retail and hospitality sectors, with a 1.5% increase in logo churn compared to Q1. Many SMBs struggle to fully utilize our platform's capabilities. We've observed that SMB customers who don't complete our initial onboarding program are 3x more likely to churn within the first six months. We've started hearing that some of our competitors, like HubSpot, have superior onboarding experience at this level. Some SMBs found our enterprise-focused features overwhelming and underutilized. They expressed a need for a more streamlined, affordable package with core functionalities relevant to their needs. We see a lot of SMB customers that are looking for something more in line with the feature set of a competitor product like Monday.com. While our enterprise platform is robust, we've identified specific feature gaps compared to competitors like Salesforce and SAP, particularly in areas like advanced AI-powered analytics and industry-specific integrations. Integrating our platform with existing legacy systems within large enterprises can be challenging and time-consuming. Delays and integration issues can lead to frustration and ultimately, churn. We lost a major pharmaceutical client, "PharmaCorp," due to a failed integration with their existing ERP system. This resulted in a loss of $500,000 ARR. Some enterprise clients felt that our customer success team wasn't providing the level of proactive, dedicated support they expected, especially during critical implementation phases. We observed higher churn rates in the EMEA region, particularly in countries with stricter data privacy regulations. Compliance concerns and the complexity of navigating regional regulations contributed to the churn. In the APAC region, we saw churn due to increased competition from local SaaS providers offering similar solutions at lower price points. We need to adjust our pricing strategy and highlight our unique value proposition to remain competitive in this market. While our North American churn is relatively low, we're seeing increased churn in the tech sector, particularly among companies that have undergone recent layoffs or restructuring. We are actively developing a streamlined, affordable package tailored to the needs of SMBs. This "Essentials" package will offer core functionalities, simplified onboarding, and a more intuitive user interface. We anticipate launching this package in Q4. We are investing heavily in developing the missing features identified by our enterprise clients, focusing on AI-powered analytics, industry-specific integrations, and enhanced security features. We are prioritizing integrations with popular enterprise platforms like Workday and ServiceNow. We are also rolling out a beta program for our AI-powered predictive analytics module, which has shown promising results in reducing churn among early adopters. We are investing in developing pre-built integrations with common ERP and CRM systems, reducing the time and complexity of onboarding for enterprise clients. We are also exploring partnerships with system integrators to provide specialized integration services. We are revamping our onboarding program to be more interactive and personalized, particularly for SMB clients. This includes providing dedicated onboarding specialists, interactive tutorials, and proactive check-ins. We are also developing a self-service knowledge base with comprehensive documentation and FAQs. We are assigning dedicated customer success managers to our key enterprise accounts, providing proactive support, regular business reviews, and personalized training. We are also implementing a 24/7 support hotline for critical issues. We are leveraging machine learning to identify customers at risk of churning. Our AI-powered churn prediction model analyzes customer usage patterns, support tickets, and feedback to identify potential churn risks. This allows us to proactively reach out to at-risk customers and address their concerns before they churn. We are implementing more frequent Net Promoter Score (NPS) and Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) surveys to gather continuous feedback and identify areas for improvement. We are also conducting post-churn interviews to understand the reasons why customers left and identify patterns. We are evaluating tiered pricing options for our SMB package to provide more flexibility and affordability. We are shifting towards a value-based pricing model for our enterprise platform, aligning pricing with the value delivered to the customer. We are adjusting our pricing strategy in the APAC region to remain competitive with local providers while highlighting our unique value proposition. We are investing in improving the stability and performance of our platform to reduce technical issues and improve the user experience. We are migrating our infrastructure to a more scalable and reliable cloud platform. We are enhancing our API to make it easier for customers to integrate our platform with other systems.

Okay, good morning everyone, and thank you for joining us today for our Q2 2024 earnings call. I'm David Miller, CEO of ConnectSphere. Today, I want to delve into a critical element of our operational performance: Sales Efficiency, specifically focusing on sales cycle length and conversion rates. These metrics are vital indicators of our go-to-market strategy effectiveness and ultimately, our ARR growth trajectory. As you know, we operate in the competitive SaaS market, specifically targeting mid-market healthcare providers with our flagship product, HealthSync EHR. We are seeing a continued healthy demand for our solutions, but increased competition, particularly from players like Salesforce Health Cloud. Therefore, optimizing our sales efficiency is paramount. In Q2, our average sales cycle length was 78 days, measured from initial lead qualification to closed-won deal. This represents a 5-day increase compared to Q1 and a 2-day increase year-over-year. Larger deals naturally involve more stakeholders, more complex negotiations, and require more rigorous security and compliance vetting, especially within the enterprise segment. For example, a deal with a major hospital system requires extensive due diligence on our HIPAA compliance and data security protocols. The current economic climate, while showing signs of stabilization, continues to exert some pressure. We're seeing increased scrutiny on ROI from potential customers, prompting more detailed proof-of-concept (POC) requests and longer evaluation periods. We have noticed that prospects are taking more time to compare our solution with the new features offered by competition. We observe significant regional differences. Our sales cycle in North America remains relatively stable at around 75 days. However, in EMEA, particularly in the DACH region, we're seeing cycles extend to an average of 90 days, primarily due to stricter data privacy regulations and more conservative purchasing behaviors. As we add features to our software, specifically our AI-powered predictive analytics module, the sales cycle lengthens because the sales team needs to demonstrate more value and address more complex technical questions. We are investing heavily in sales enablement programs, including enhanced product training and sales playbooks. We recently launched a new "Value Selling" program specifically designed to help our sales reps articulate the ROI of our solution more effectively. We are expanding our technical pre-sales team to provide more hands-on support during POCs and technical evaluations. This team is now equipped with pre-built integration demos. We are strengthening our partnerships with system integrators and consulting firms, particularly in EMEA. These partners can help us navigate local regulations and build trust with potential customers, ultimately shortening the sales cycle. In Marketing, we're refining our lead qualification process to ensure we're focusing our sales efforts on the most promising prospects. We're leveraging data analytics to identify key indicators of buyer intent and prioritize leads accordingly. Our overall conversion rate, defined as the percentage of qualified leads that convert into paying customers, was 28% in Q2. This is slightly down from 30% in Q1, but remains within our target range of 25-30%. We are closely monitoring conversion rates at each stage of the sales funnel. We've identified that the biggest drop-off occurs between the "Demo" stage and the "Proposal" stage. This suggests that we need to improve the effectiveness of our demos and tailor our proposals more closely to the specific needs of each prospect. Conversion rates vary significantly depending on the customer segment. For example, our conversion rate for enterprise customers is typically lower (around 22%) due to the longer sales cycles and more complex decision-making processes. However, the higher average deal size for enterprise customers more than compensates for the lower conversion rate. We offer a free trial of HealthSync EHR with limited functionality. Customers who engage with the free trial have a significantly higher conversion rate compared to those who don't. Therefore, we are focusing on driving greater adoption of the free trial program. We are emphasizing a more personalized sales approach, tailoring our messaging and demonstrations to the specific needs and pain points of each prospect. We are revamping our demo process to make it more interactive and engaging. We are incorporating more real-world use cases and focusing on showcasing the value of our key features. We are investing in content marketing to educate potential customers about the benefits of our solution and build trust. We are conducting A/B testing on our sales collateral, email campaigns, and website landing pages to optimize our messaging and improve conversion rates.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Emily Carter to discuss the financials in more detail.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $340 million, representing a 27% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 75%, and operating income was $63 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $1.35 billion to $1.37 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Lee for a technology update.

Michael Lee:
Thank you, Emily. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Jessica Davis will provide update on product roadmap.

Jessica Davis:
Thank you, Michael. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of SynergyAssist. This new feature significantly improves the efficiency of healthcare providers by automating administrative tasks. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature which aligns with our product strategy.

Laura Garcia:
Thank you, Jessica. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 18% increase in website traffic and a 22% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Kim with Goldman Sachs.

John Kim:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of SynergyCloud on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, and what's the competitive landscape like?

Robert Jones:
